title: Simulation of Full-Wave Rectifier in MATLAB/Simulink

questions.q: What is the main advantage of a Full-Wave Bridge Rectifier over a Half-Wave Rectifier?
questions.a: It utilizes both half-cycles of the AC input, doubling the DC output voltage and efficiency (81.2% vs 40.6%) and lowering the ripple factor (0.482 vs 1.21) without requiring a center-tapped transformer.

questions.q: Why is the peak output voltage of a silicon bridge rectifier `Vm - 1.4 V` instead of `Vm - 0.7 V`?
questions.a: Because in every half-cycle, current flows through two silicon diodes in series with the load resistor, dropping 2 * 0.7 V = 1.4 V.

questions.q: Which diodes conduct during the positive and negative half-cycles in a 4-diode bridge?
questions.a: Two diagonally opposite diodes conduct during the positive half-cycle, and the other two diagonally opposite diodes conduct during the negative half-cycle.

questions.q: What is the Peak Inverse Voltage (PIV) of each diode in a Full-Wave Bridge Rectifier?
questions.a: PIV = V_m (compared to 2*V_m for a center-tapped full-wave rectifier).

questions.q: Why is the output ripple frequency 100 Hz when the input AC frequency is 50 Hz?
questions.a: Because the negative half-cycle is inverted into a second positive pulse every period, producing two pulses per 20 ms input cycle (period = 10 ms -> 100 Hz).

questions.q: In a SPICE simulation of a bridge rectifier, why can't both V1's negative terminal and the load resistor's negative terminal be tied to `GND` simultaneously?
questions.a: Tying both to `GND` would short-circuit one of the lower bridge diodes. Either V1 must float between two non-ground AC nodes or the load voltage must be measured differentially.

questions.q: How many diodes are required in a bridge rectifier versus a center-tapped full-wave rectifier?
questions.a: A bridge rectifier requires 4 diodes (no center tap needed), whereas a center-tapped rectifier uses 2 diodes but requires a center-tapped transformer.

questions.q: For a 20 V peak AC source and a silicon bridge rectifier, calculate V_peak_out and V_dc (unfiltered).
If one diode in a 4-diode bridge rectifier fails open-circuit, what does the output waveform look like?
questions.a: One half-cycle stops conducting, so the bridge rectifier degrades into a half-wave rectifier.

questions.q: Why is a capacitor filter more effective on a full-wave rectifier than on a half-wave rectifier?
questions.a: Because the ripple frequency is twice as high (100 Hz vs 50 Hz), giving the capacitor only half as much time (10 ms vs 20 ms) to discharge between peaks.
